obligation: Acquirer notice of suspected card data compromise (contractual)
citation: Merchant agreement with the acquiring bank (fictional term); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 12.10 (N44-45-R01)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of card data, including a common point of purchase notice from the acquirer or processor
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspecting a compromise (merchant agreement term). Clock starts at suspicion, not confirmation

obligation: Card brand compromise procedures, including forensic investigation (contractual)
citation: Payment brand operating rules, applied through the acquirer - not law
trigger: Acquirer or card brand opens a compromise case
deadline: Per acquirer and brand instructions (not verified); may require a PCI Forensic Investigator
notify: Acquirer; card brands through the acquirer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - follow acquirer instructions; brand rules were not verified

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents. Personal information includes a name with a credit or debit card number and any required security code, and an email address with a password for an online account (501.171(1)(g))
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - expected for skimmed cards with security codes

trigger: Law enforcement agency determines notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies; keep the request in writing

trigger: After appropriate investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Document the determination, keep it 5 years, and provide it to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely for skimmed card data; counsel decides

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A third-party agent (for example the storefront vendor or processor) has a breach of the company's personal information
deadline: No later than 10 days following the determination of the breach

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents of other states (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example without unreasonable delay or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected cardholders reside (for example seasonal residents)

trigger: Suspected criminal compromise of card data
notify: FBI (IC3) or U.S. Secret Service field office

deadline: Per policy (use the carrier breach hotline before hiring vendors)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if an extortion demand is made. All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event (unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information)
trigger: Notification event at a financial institution involving 500+ consumers
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 30 days after discovery
notify: FTC via online form at ftc.gov
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company issues no credit and is not a financial institution under Part 314

obligation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident disclosure
trigger: Registrant determines an incident is material
deadline: Within four business days after determining the incident is material

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). Proposed scope: critical infrastructure entities above the SBA size standard, or meeting a sector criterion regardless of size; the company is below its SBA size standard

citation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or Kaspersky covered article in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts
